newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN SHARES STABLE AT LOWER LEVELS PRE-BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN SHARES STABLE AT LOWER LEVELS PRE-BOURSE.

text.p: German shares fell sharply in early pre-bourse trade on Monday, with trading sentiment in electronic trade badly hit by a 1.91 percent slide on Wall Street on Friday and a weaker dollar.

The IBIS DAX index proved resolute in the face of the Wall Street losses, and after sliding to 4,267.74 points early on, recouped losses to stand at 4,309.60 points pre-bourse, down 0.74 percent or 32.23 points.
"The sell-off this morning was on the back of Wall Street and the dollar, but it has been squeezing back since that. Not exactly a huge correction," a Frankfurt broker said.

"People were keeping an eye on the Bund this morning and the fact that it is positive has helped to stabilise things in the equity market. But generally this is real Monday morning stuff, volumes are thin and you have traders selling off from Friday," he said.
Among the winners this morning were shares in German steelmakers Friedrich Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp FHKG.F and Thyssen AG. Both shares were among the top gainers after reports they planned to merge.
Krupp rose up 12.10 marks, or 3.77 percent, at 333 marks, while Thyssen rose 10.30 marks, or 2.48 percent, at 426 marks.
The Spiegel news magazine reported in its Monday edition that the two groups were stepping up merger talks, having agreed earlier this year to merge their flat steel businesses.
On the downside, shares in pharmaceuticals group Altana AG were the biggest losers.

Altana shares were down 13 marks, or 7.98 percent, at 150 marks. Dealers said there was speculation in the market about problems about the further development of its Pantoprazol product, but no-one at Altana was available for comment.
The speculation hit Altana shares last week as well. Shares in Altana fell 12 percent to 163 marks on Friday.
Dealers said they were looking ahead to interim figures from German chemical companies this week, as well as watching Wall Street for further inspiration.

U.S. data this week include unit labour costs and productivity for the second quarter on Tuesday as well as July retail sales and producer prices on Wednesday. Thursday sees the release of weekly jobless claims and July consumer prices.
